reported_runtime_input_from_root: Attempt001 deadline, frames_out1/frames_in0/packets0 and no captured READY/TX; recovery verified Linux. Raw capture was not independently inspected here.
diagnosis: Pinned ARM console supports d_select readiness but its major lacks the kqueue opt-in required by poll. The poll-created filter fails registration and maps to POLLNVAL; guest ignores that console result and waits solely for POLLOUT before its first write. Both queued READY and encoded OPEN can therefore remain unwritten until deadline. frames_out1 is a queue fact, not an actual transmitted frame.

evidence.fact: READY and OPEN are queued; frames_out counts encoded/queued frames. Actual stdout writes require POLLOUT at477; console POLLNVAL is ignored.
poll registers EV_POLL kqueue read/write filters; registration error maps to POLLNVAL at1791. No NOTE_LOWAT/data1 supplied.
vn_kqfilter routes character-device read/write filters through spec_kqfilter.
spec_kqfilter reads per-major CDEVSW_SELECT_KQUEUE; unflagged console uses EVFILTID_SPEC.
filt_specattach rejects unflagged devices without explicit NOTE_LOWAT and data1, setting EINVAL.
console major0 uses cnselect; default km major12 uses ttselect. cdevsw_flags global array is zero initialized at224.
cnselect delegates to the active constty device or km_tty[0], separately from cnwrite at128.
kmwrite calls line-discipline l_write; kmstart/kmoutput drain console output.
ttyselect FWRITE returns a positive available count when queue<=lowat and TS_CONNECTED; read uses ttnread and selrecord.
select selscan uses FREAD/FWRITE and calls fo_select at1654; it does not require vnode kqueue attach.
vn_select calls VNOP_SELECT; spec_select at spec_vnops920 calls actual cdev d_select.
soo_select implements socket soreadable/sowriteable and readiness wait registration.
vnode write maps FNONBLOCK to IO_NDELAY before device write; independent of poll registration.

registration_search: Pinned XNU cdevsw_setkqueueok call sites found for oslog7/8 and PTY drivers, none console0/km12; cdevsw_flags0 is not explicitly initialized or set in inspected pinned XNU. No claim about a newly observed runtime flag/readiness value.
narrow_correction: New isolated revision only: use select() for the same five endpoints, rebuild fd_sets and20ms timeval each iteration, guard every active FD against FD_SETSIZE, preserve queue/partial-write/EOF/SO_ERROR/deadline/cleanup logic. Do not assume POLLOUT from device write capability or replace it with speculative reads. No kernel/m1n1 change is needed for this source correction.
